recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. If the work group wants to replace the HTTP Category approach or define the `http://hl7.org/fhir/tag/security` scheme, handle that through a new or existing final tracker such as the unresolved BTG maturity discussion rather than this applied clarification.
issue_request: Applied/Persuasive Security WG request to clarify the Break the Glass example on the security-labels page: fix broken Category/security-label URLs, show clearer purpose-of-use Category syntax, and consider a `_purpose` query parameter.
initial_application: Source history shows the original broken BTG Category value was changed to `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/v3-ActReason#BTG` in commit 7223a0014e. Later 2023 commits tied to FHIR-42756 and FHIR-42757 corrected the BTG terminology URL, updated links and wording, and added OAuth purpose-of-use guidance alongside the HTTP Category example.
additional_context: The active build includes `security-labels.html` and `security.html`. Later Applied issue FHIR-53885 moved BTG content from Security Labels to the Security page, preserving the OAuth and HTTP Category examples. The linked Zulip thread shows `_purpose`, OAuth/JWT/SAML, and per-request header options were discussed without a single settled replacement, and John Moehrke noted a query parameter would not cover create, update, and delete. A terminology thread confirms the current BTG Category value is the intended terminology CodeSystem URI while the remaining `tag/security` scheme is a broader unresolved design point. FHIR-53925 is still Triaged on BTG maturity, so it is not a final source-edit instruction.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current Security page already provides the corrected BTG code URL, explains BTG as a purpose of use, gives OAuth and HTTP Category declaration examples, and states that FHIR does not define the surrounding policy or protocol. Adding POPHLTH, inventing `_purpose`, or redefining/removing the experimental Category-header scheme would exceed the final FHIR-19499 decision.
